correctness.rationale: For independent exponential rates \(a,a,b\), the exact survival is \(S=2x-x^2+x^r(1-x)^2\), with \(x=e^{-at}\) and \(r=b/a\). Exact differentiation gives \(D=(S\prime)^2-S S\prime\prime =x[2x^2+x^rB_r+2x^{2r}(1-x)^2]\), where \(h\prime=a^2D/S^2\). For \(0<r<2\), \(r\ne1\), one has \(D/x^{r+1}\to-2(r-1)^2\). At \(r=1\), the exact positive factorization is \(D=3x^3(3-x)(1-x)\). For \(r\ge2\), an exponential lower bound and two logarithmic inequalities prove \(2e^{(r-2)at}+B_r>0\) for every \(t>0\), proving strict positivity of \(D\). The packaged standalone exact-rational verifier passed 3,344 algebraic identities, 2,190 integer-rate signs and two rational negative-tail witnesses. Infinite-time and real-parameter quantifiers are proved analytically, not inferred from finite grids. Leading asymptotic constants follow from the same exact identity.

value.rationale: The natural three-component heterogeneous family with two repeated exponential rates has a sharp, nonmonotone age-dependent hazard phase diagram: equal-rate IFR, immediate failure under mild heterogeneity and strict IFR re-entry only when the third rate doubles the repeated rate. This resolves a substantive shape classification in parallel reliability, useful when selecting models permitting monotone failure-risk assumptions. The result is a global iff and exact negative-tail obstruction rather than an isolated numeric example. Scope is intentionally exactly three components with two equal rates; neither arbitrary triples nor dependent failures are claimed.
